column1: # G3 phase 4: deprecate(x, m) -- the deprecation mark
# unification-TRANSPARENT: the value unifies exactly as x, and the
# record m (keys msg/use/since, all optional, values strings; `use` is
# a path spelled as a STRING) rides the result through meets, reference
# clones and spread applications. Canon renders the call back
# reparseably; generation is unchanged. The point-of-use surfaces: a
# vet `deprecated` finding at severity warning (rows below), the LSP
# Deprecated tag, and the breaking verb's --allow-deprecated-removal
# Every expectation was obtained by the parity probe (AGENTS.md).
# The meet keeps the record whichever side carries it -- order-free.
# Two records meet as their key-wise union (G12 phase 8, ADR-052),
# rendered as nested calls, one record per layer of values.
# A reference clones its target, record included: q's use of p is a
# A deprecated spread template deprecates every key it governs.
# The record's vocabulary is msg/use/since; other keys are DROPPED, not
# carried -- the record is a contract the tooling reads, not a second
# Generation is unchanged: the mark never reaches the output.
# Arity: the value, and its optional record -- nothing else.
# The point-of-use warning (severity `warning`, class compat, the slot
# G2 reserved): the verdict is UNTOUCHED -- a deprecated use is valid,
# and the report says so while saying it is deprecated.
# Two records on one value are one deprecation, so one warning.
# A conflict on a deprecated value reports the CONFLICT: the nil
# replaced the value, so there is no deprecated survivor to warn about.
# Top carries a deprecation as any value does.
# --- A deprecation inside a recursive alias (G12 phase 16) -------------
# The alias stays its name in the site, and a finding inside a
# declaration spells the alias without its scope.
